items.title: Andrea Stella explains how qualifying destroyed McLaren’s Mexico GP: “We paid the price”
items.summary: Having a podium-capable car means much less if you spend 71 laps hopelessly trapped in dirty air. That was the reality for McLaren at the Mexico City Grand Prix. A difficult Saturday qualifying session left the Woking garage entirely on the back foot, completely negating the raw race pace of its machinery.

items.title: Charles Leclerc brushes off Lewis Hamilton clash: “I could be unhappy too”
items.summary: The opening lap of the Mexico City Grand Prix featured an intense, intra-team battle within Ferrari. Battling for the race lead, Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton traded heavy, aggressive blows through the opening sequence of corners.

items.title: Colton Herta to run Cadillac FP1 in Brazil as FIA superlicense quest continues
items.summary: Cadillac test driver Colton Herta will conduct his sixth Friday practice session of the F1 season at this weekend's Sao Paulo GP to collect his missing FIA superlicense point required to race in the series. Herta, who has been building up for an F1 campaign with private testing, FP1 sessions and a troubled F2 campaign, needs 40 points to obtain the required FIA superlicense.

items.title: Mercedes boss praises Antonelli’s masterclass while admitting they failed George Russell
items.summary: The Brackley garage experienced the absolute extremes of motorsport at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodríguez. While the team successfully crowned the youngest world drivers' champion in Formula 1 history on Sunday, the engineering brass was simultaneously forced to publicly apologise to the other side of the garage for a mechanical failure.

items.title: Rafa Camara to debut in F1 Brazil GP as Esteban Ocon out at Haas
items.summary: The Haas F1 team has decided Esteban Ocon will not race again for the squad, with 2027 debutant Rafa Camara getting an early debut this weekend on home soil. Following increasingly strained relations between Ocon and the team, a heated argument in Mexico proved the final straw that made team principal Ayao Komatsu decide to bench the Frenchman.

items.title: The 'difference' between Kimi Antonelli's F1 title and Lewis Hamilton's according to Toto Wolff
items.summary: Mercedes boss Toto Wolff has explained how “different” it felt watching Kimi Antonelli become Formula 1 world champion compared to his record-breaking years with Lewis Hamilton. Antonelli clinched his maiden title in Mexico on Sunday to become F1’s youngest ever world champion at the age of only 20, thanks to a dominant 2026 with four rounds still remaining.

items.title: McLaren to introduce 2027 F1 front wing at Brazil GP
items.summary: McLaren will introduce upgrades to its MCL40 Formula 1 car at this weekend’s Brazil Grand Prix, featuring a front wing concept which is expected to feature on its 2027 challenger.

items.title: Red Bull's rumoured €27million deal takes shape in leaked Max Verstappen shoot
items.summary: A commercial production shoot just accidentally poured gasoline on one of the biggest off-track rumours in the Formula 1 paddock right now. Leaked photographs circulating across social media show Max Verstappen casually resting on the front left wheel of his RB22 while sporting what is expected to be an unreleased team kit.

items.title: Isack Hadjar rues missed opportunity after George Russell clash at Mexico GP
items.summary: Nailing the launch of your life only to get pushed off the track a few corners later is a surefire way to ruin a Sunday. Just ask Isack Hadjar. Starting seventh on the grid at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez, the Red Bull driver executed a flawless getaway.

items.title: Marco Antonelli: "I saw the champion in Kimi after his Australia crash"
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli became Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion at the Mexico City Grand Prix, becoming the first Italian to win the title since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

items.title: Why Honda’s power unit lasted barely five laps in F1 Mexico GP
items.summary: In its Mexico Grand Prix preview, Honda’s Shintaro Orihara had described Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez as “a very challenging track for the power unit”, but he perhaps didn’t expect Aston Martin’s weekend to go so awry.

items.title: How Red Bull's crucial strategy call helped Max Verstappen win the "Maxico Grand Prix"
items.summary: Although Sunday at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez was above all Kimi Antonelli's day, there were naturally two other major storylines in the Formula 1 paddock: the tensions at Ferrari and how Fred Vasseur will manage them, plus Max Verstappen's sixth victory in Mexico.

items.title: Isack Hadjar blames himself for George Russell clash that “ruined” his Mexico GP
items.summary: Isack Hadjar has taken some responsibility for his collision with George Russell at Formula 1’s Mexico GP, in which he miraculously scored two points. Hadjar qualified down in seventh at Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, two tenths and three spots away from Red Bull team-mate Max Verstappen, but gained two positions courtesy of a decent start.

items.title: Kimi Antonelli labels the "turning point" in F1 title-winning season
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli has labelled the Japanese Grand Prix as the “turning point” in his title-clinching Formula 1 season - saying that win gave him the belief he could become world champion. The Mercedes driver clinched his maiden title in Mexico on Sunday after a dominant 2026 season, yielding nine wins and 16 podiums with still four rounds remaining.

items.title: Lewis Hamilton goes viral after emotional moment with Peter Bonnington in Mexico
items.summary: Formula 1 fans have praised seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton after footage of him congratulating his former Mercedes race engineer Peter 'Bono' Bonnington at the Mexican Grand Prix went viral. Hamilton worked with Bonnington throughout his time at the Brackley outfit, where he secured six of his seven championships.

items.title: George Russell breaks silence with heartfelt message after Kimi Antonelli's F1 title win
items.summary: George Russell has shared a heartfelt message after missing media duties following the Mexican Grand Prix. The Briton admitted that "2026 was not meant to be my year" in a long message to his fans on social media after his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli claimed his maiden championship at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez.

items.title: Peter Bonnington reveals "stern conversation" that transformed Kimi Antonelli's F1 career
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli's race engineer Peter 'Bono' Bonnington has revealed that a "really stern conversation" helped turn around the Italian driver's rookie Formula 1 season, a year before he became the 2026 world champion. Antonelli finished third at last weekend's Mexican Grand Prix, which was enough to secure his maiden title.

items.title: Juan Pablo Montoya demands "consequences" for Ferrari drivers after Mexican GP disaster
items.summary: Former Formula 1 driver and F1 TV pundit Juan Pablo Montoya has argued that there must be "consequences" for Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc after their first-lap battle likely cost Ferrari the win at the Mexican Grand Prix. Both drivers ran wide when Leclerc attempted to overtake Hamilton, who had started from pole position.

items.title: Cadillac to investigate high-speed Mexico GP failure that led to angry Valtteri Bottas reaction
items.summary: Cadillac Formula 1 team principal Marcin Budkowski has vowed to ensure accidents like the one that ended Valtteri Bottas' Mexico Grand Prix "do not happen again". Bottas was at top speed entering Turn 1 on lap 46 at the Autodromo Hermanos Rogriguez when his front-left suspension collapsed as he hit the brakes, sending the Finn into a slide and into the TecPro barrier.

items.title: How Mercedes can win the 2026 F1 constructors' championship at the Brazilian GP
items.summary: Mercedes has the opportunity to claim the Formula 1 constructors' championship at this weekend's Brazilian Grand Prix, one week after Kimi Antonelli clinched the drivers' title in Mexico. Heading into the race weekend in Sao Paulo, Mercedes leads the standings by 126 points over second-placed Ferrari. How can Mercedes win the 2026 F1 constructors' championship in Brazil?

items.title: What was Kimi Antonelli’s best moment of his F1 title-winning campaign? Our writers have their say
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli’s record-breaking Formula 1 world championship triumph was highlighted by many superb performances. But which one was his best? Antonelli duly wrapped up his maiden F1 crown in Mexico with four rounds to spare – becoming the youngest-ever world champion in the process.

items.title: Toto Wolff explains George Russell's media absence after Mexican GP disappointment
items.summary: Mercedes Formula 1 team principal and CEO Toto Wolff described the Mexican Grand Prix as a "catastrophic moment" for George Russell. The Briton started second on the grid after qualifying just 0.009 seconds behind Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, but immediately lost ground. He was then also given a 10-second penalty for a first-lap collision with Red Bull's Isack Hadjar.

items.title: Mercedes fined for George Russell skipping F1 Mexico GP media duties
items.summary: Mercedes was fined €5,000 following the Mexico Grand Prix after George Russell failed to attend his post-race Formula 1 media commitments. The Mercedes driver finished sixth at Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez despite starting Sunday’s race in second, having dropped four positions on lap one due to a poor battery.

items.title: Kimi Antonelli reveals why he won’t take number 1 for the 2027 F1 season
items.summary: The number 1 will not be seen on the Formula 1 grid next season for the first time since 2021. Max Verstappen and Lando Norris have consistently decided to take the opportunity to claim number 1 after winning their world titles, but Antonelli will not do so.

items.title: Fred Vasseur calls for "respect" after Lewis Hamilton-Charles Leclerc Mexican GP clash
items.summary: Ferrari Formula 1 team principal Fred Vasseur said the first-lap clash between his drivers, Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc, at the Mexican Grand Prix comes down to "a matter of respect". Leclerc attempted to overtake Hamilton, who had started the race at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez from pole position, at Turn 4. Both drivers went off the track and Leclerc came out ahead.

items.title: Toto Wolff hits out at F1’s “entitled” drivers and “endless moaners on the radio”
items.summary: After a stunning championship win from his young driver Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has criticised the "entitled" drivers and "endless moaners on the radio" in Formula 1. He believes this year's world champion should be a role model for them.

items.title: Who slept best last night: Kimi Antonelli
items.summary: Where do you start when trying to digest Kimi Antonelli's championship? What do you say about it? Perhaps start with the numbers. This victory is historic. He's not just the youngest to win the F1 title; he's beaten the previous record by more than three years. He's done it with an almost perfect season, just his second in F1.

items.title: Kimi Antonelli wants special photo with Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen on his wall after F1 title
items.summary: The 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix is one for the history books: Kimi Antonelli has been crowned the youngest world champion of all time, and partly because of the superlicence rules, that record will certainly not be an easy one to break.

items.title: Who slept worst last night: Frederic Vasseur
items.summary: There was at least one moment during Frederic Vasseur's post-Mexican Grand Prix media briefing when the Ferrari team principal burst into laughter. Motorsport Network journalist Ronald Vording had just asked him what felt like the umpteenth question about the evidently strained atmosphere following the first-lap clash between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc.

items.title: Penalty drops Oscar Piastri out of F1 Mexico GP points
items.summary: Oscar Piastri’s tough Mexico Grand Prix weekend has ended in point-less fashion, after the McLaren Formula 1 driver copped a penalty for his collision with Arvid Lindblad. Piastri’s 60-strong streak of Q3 appearances (including sprints) ended at Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez as he qualified a lowly 12th, which paved the way for his troubles in the midfield.
